production.note: US model year 2014: Car and Driver tested a '2014 Ferrari LaFerrari' (read by the project owner on 9 October 2026 (the site blocks the research tools)); an earlier pass (3 October 2026) found the EPA listing (via MPG Buddy) for 2014 only (that page would not open on 9 October). Kelley Blue Book also has a 2015 page ('2014 features shown. 2015 may differ.', kbb-laferrari), so a 2015 model year is possible and unconfirmed. Ferrari unveiled the car in March 2013 (supercars-net-laferrari-release); 499 were built.

body.note: Two-seat fixed-roof mid-engined car; the open Aperta is a separate model.

displacementL.note: 6,262 cc. Ferrari release: 'a 6262 cc V12'; Evo panel: 'V12, 6262cc, plus 160bhp electric motor' (evo-laferrari); 2LUXURY2 spec list: 'Total displacement 6262 cc' (2luxury2-laferrari). Car and Driver (owner-read): '6.3-liter V-12'.

aspiration.note: Car and Driver (owner-read): 'DOHC 48-valve 6.3-liter V-12'; no turbocharger or supercharger.

fuel.note: HY-KERS hybrid (V12 plus electric motor; 'the batteries weigh just 60 kg'); not a plug-in.

drivetrain.note: Mid-engined, rear-driven ('ideal weight distribution (59% at the rear)'); rear-wheel drive inferred from the description.

transmission.note: Ferrari release: 'the F1 dual-clutch gearbox'; 2LUXURY2 spec list: '7-speed DCT' (2luxury2-laferrari); Car and Driver (owner-read): '7-speed dual-clutch automatic'.

powerHp.note: Ferrari's combined system rating. Quote (Ferrari press release reproduced by Supercars.net, credited '[Source: Ferrari SpA]'): "giving it a combined power output of 963 CV". 963 CV x 0.98632 = 950 hp. 2LUXURY2 spec list: 'V12 maximum power* 800 CV @9000 rpm', 'Electric motor output 120 Kw (163 CV)', 'Total maximum power 963 CV' (2luxury2-laferrari). Car and Driver (owner-read, caranddriver-laferrari-test): 'combined system, 950 hp' (V-12 789 hp, motor 161 hp); Evo panel: 'Max power: 950bhp' (evo-laferrari). No separate US SAE rating was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS.

weightLb.note: Weight-order step 2: Car and Driver road-test curb weight (owner decision, 9 October 2026, docs/DATA_GUIDE.md). Owner decision, 9 October 2026: Car and Driver's tested figure used. Car and Driver road test of a 2014 car, read by the project owner on 9 October 2026 (the site blocks the research tools): "Curb weight: 3489 lb" (1,583 kg; a measured weight, labelled tested). Ferrari published no weight. Two databases agree (ultimatespecs and dimensions.com, 1,585 kg, owner-found 5 October 2026), but the magazines' kerb figures are 1,410-1,430 kg; see discrepancies.

sources.title: Ferrari LaFerrari hypercar tested review (C/D test results)

sources.publisher: Ferrari S.p.A. (press release reproduced by Supercars.net)
sources.title: LaFerrari – Official Press Release and Photos

values.value: 1,410 kg (3,109 lb): 'a proper, comparable with fluids kerb weight'

discrepancies.reason: Unexplained. Ferrari published no weight; the European magazines' kerb figures are about 11-12% below Car and Driver's scale weight and KBB's figure is lower still. Databases (ultimatespecs, dimensions.com) give 1,585 kg, close to Car and Driver.
discrepancies.resolution: Owner decision, 9 October 2026: Car and Driver's tested figure used. Provisional until a Ferrari kerb weight or a magazine specification panel labelled kerb/curb is found.

reviewNotes: Weight conflict (tested 1,583 kg vs magazine kerb 1,410-1,430 kg) is settled by owner decision, not explained. US model years: 2014 confirmed only by Car and Driver's test title and an earlier EPA check; KBB also lists 2015.
